strings.name: Jeffrey Sachs
strings.summary: Sachs moved from Harvard economics into policy advice on transitions in Bolivia, Poland and the former Soviet region, where rapid-reform approaches remain contested. He joined Columbia in 2002 and broadened his work to poverty, public health and sustainability. He led the UN Millennium Project, participates in the Sustainable Development Solutions Network and continues to engage in international policy debates.

strings.highlights.h1.text: Worked on debt, hyperinflation and transitions from planning; reform paths and social consequences remain contested.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Global development
strings.highlights.h2.text: Led the UN Millennium Project and contributes to sustainable-development goals, poverty and public-health research.

strings.timeline.t3.title: Helped build SDSN

strings.timeline.t5.title: Joined Columbia
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became Earth Institute director and led the UN Millennium Project.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Advised Polish reforms
strings.timeline.t6.text: Advised Poland on its transition from central planning to a market economy.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Advised Bolivian stabilization
strings.timeline.t7.text: Advised on hyperinflation; the policies’ social consequences have been debated.
